mainTopic: ביטול רשות: whether rights may be given up and then given back (the dispute between רב and שמואל and its possible sources among the תנאים), and the status of a צדוקי in the laws of עירוב.
overview: רבא was asked to give up his courtyard rights so hot water could be carried for a baby's ברית מילה, and then have the rights given back to him, as רב allows. רבא answers that on this point he holds like שמואל, who forbids giving rights back. When challenged that שמואל's reason should also forbid ביטול רשות between courtyards, רבא explains that שמואל's real reason is to keep rabbinic law from looking like a joke. The גמרא then looks at the dispute between רב and שמואל on its own. It tries to tie it to the dispute between רבי אליעזר and רבנן, and then to the dispute between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה about someone who carried after giving up his rights. Each link is pushed aside, though רב אשי insists the first link is correct. Next the גמרא turns to the משנה's story of a צדוקי neighbor. It explains that words are missing: there is a dispute over whether a צדוקי is like a גוי, and רבן גמליאל says he is not. A ברייתא gives two versions of רבן גמליאל's words to his sons, one from רבי מאיר and one from רבי יהודה. The amud ends with the גמרא questioning what רבי מאיר's version implies about who carries first; the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: A plan: give up your rights, then get them back
steps.stepSummary: The questioner suggests that רבא give up his rights to the other courtyard's residents so the water can be moved. Afterward, they would give the rights back to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the Master stay where he is and give up his rights to them. Then let them turn around and give up their rights back to the Master.
steps.whatsHappening: Someone proposes a two-part plan to solve the hot-water problem. רבא gives up his rights now, and the others give them back later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once רבא gives up his rights, the other residents can carry freely and bring the water. But then רבא himself could not carry in his courtyard. So the plan adds a second step: the others give their rights back to him afterward.

keyTerms.meaning: Let the Master sit/stay in his place
Let him give up (his rights)
Let them turn around / go back
The Master (a respectful way to say 'you')

phrases.english: Let the Master stay in his place,
and give up [his rights] to them,
phrases.notes: Meaning the residents of the baby's courtyard.

phrases.english: and then let them in turn give up [their rights] to the Master,
phrases.notes: This is the second step, done after the water has been moved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier story of the baby's hot water, which comes on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Proposal: רבא gives up his rights so the water can be moved, and then the rights are given back to him.

steps.title: Support for the plan from רב
steps.stepSummary: The questioner backs up the plan with רב's ruling that one may give up rights and then have them given back.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רב said: One may give up rights, and then turn around and give them up again.
steps.whatsHappening: The questioner shows that the plan is legal by quoting רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב allows ביטול רשות to go back and forth: first A gives to B, then B gives back to A. That is exactly the second half of the plan in step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: We may give up (rights in the courtyard)
And then go back and give up again (in the reverse direction)
For indeed / since

phrases.english: For Rav said:
phrases.notes: Introduces the source that supports the plan.

phrases.english: One may renounce, and then go back and renounce [in reverse].
phrases.notes: One person gives up rights to the other, and later the other gives them back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the legal basis for the second half of the plan in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That the rights can be given back to רבא after the water is moved.

steps.title: רבא holds like שמואל on this point
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects the plan. On giving rights back, he follows שמואל, who forbids it.
steps.simpleTranslation: I, in this matter, hold like שמואל, who said: One may not give up rights and then turn around and give them up again.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא says the plan won't work for him. He does not follow רב on this point; he follows שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under שמואל's view, once רבא gives up his rights, they cannot be handed back to him. The second half of the plan falls apart, so רבא rejects it.

keyTerms.meaning: I, in this matter
I hold / that is my opinion
One may not give up (and then reverse it)

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying that ביטול רשות never works. He only rejects the back-and-forth: giving up rights and then getting them back.

phrases.english: I, in this matter, hold like Shmuel,
phrases.notes: 'In this matter' shows that רבא doesn't follow שמואל on everything, just here.

phrases.english: who said: One may not renounce
and then go back and renounce [in reverse].
phrases.notes: The rights cannot be handed back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from רב by siding with שמואל.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the second half of the plan (giving the rights back), not ביטול רשות in general.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The plan relies on רב, but רבא rules like שמואל on this point.

steps.title: Aren't both rules based on the same reason?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא argues that שמואל's ban on giving rights back seems to come from the same reason as the ban on giving rights from one courtyard to another. If so, רבא should not give up his rights here at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it one reason? Why can't one give up rights and then give them back? Isn't it because once he gave up his rights, he left this courtyard completely? Then he is like a resident of a different courtyard, and there is no giving up of rights from one courtyard to another. So the Master also should not give up his rights.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא challenges רבא for being inconsistent. If רבא accepts שמואל's reasoning in one place, he should accept it in the other too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggested reason for שמואל's rule is this: after giving up his rights, the person counts as an outsider from another חצר. Rights cannot be passed from one חצר to another, so the outsider cannot receive them back. But that same principle would also stop רבא from giving his rights to the neighboring courtyard in the first place. So רבא cannot follow שמואל in one rule and ignore him in the other.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it one and the same reason?
He removed himself / withdrew
Like a resident of a different courtyard
Rights cannot be given up from one courtyard to another

phrases.english: But isn't it one [and the same] reason?
phrases.notes: A question that is really a challenge.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא אֵין מְבַטְּלִין וְחוֹזְרִין וּמְבַטְּלִין —
phrases.english: What is the reason one may not renounce and then renounce back?
Is it not because once he renounced his rights,
he removed himself from here completely,
phrases.notes: He is treated as if he no longer lives in this courtyard.

phrases.english: and he becomes like a resident of another courtyard,
and there is no renouncing of rights from courtyard to courtyard.
phrases.notes: This is שמואל's position on courtyard-to-courtyard ביטול.

phrases.english: [So] the Master too should not renounce.
phrases.notes: רבא should not give up his rights to the neighboring courtyard either.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's answer in step 3 for being inconsistent.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's choice to follow שמואל on giving rights back while still being willing to give up rights to another courtyard.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both rules seem to rest on one principle: a person who gives up his rights becomes an outsider, and rights cannot pass between courtyards. Accepting one rule means accepting the other.

steps.title: שמואל's real reason: not making the rabbinic law look like a joke
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that שמואל's reason is different. Passing rights back and forth would make the enactment of the חכמים look ridiculous.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, this is the reason: so that the rabbinic rule should not become something to laugh at and mock.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends himself by giving a different reason for שמואל's rule. He explains that the two rules are not linked after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל forbids giving rights back not because the person becomes an outsider, but because constant back-and-forth would turn the laws of עירוב into a game. Since that reason has nothing to do with the courtyard-to-courtyard question, רבא can follow שמואל here and still give up his rights to another courtyard.

keyTerms.meaning: There, this is the reason
So that ... not
A rabbinic matter / enactment
Laughter and mockery

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's ban on giving rights back is based on protecting the dignity of rabbinic law. It is not based on treating the person as a resident of another courtyard. So it does not force רבא to also ban ביטול רשות between courtyards.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how the גמרא can separate two rules that seem to share one reason. Once a different reason is identified, a person can hold one rule without being forced into the other.

phrases.english: There, this is the reason:
phrases.notes: 'There' refers to שמואל's rule against giving rights back.

phrases.english: so that it should not be
that the words of the Sages become like laughter and mockery.
phrases.notes: Passing rights back and forth would make the Sages' rule look meaningless.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4 by giving a different reason.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different underlying reason (separates the two rules)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל's rule came from treating the person as a resident of another courtyard, which would also ban courtyard-to-courtyard ביטול.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל's rule comes from not making rabbinic law look ridiculous, so it does not affect courtyard-to-courtyard ביטול.

steps.title: Restating the dispute between רב and שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the earlier ruling. רב allows giving up rights and then having them given back. שמואל forbids it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Back to the matter itself: רב said one may give up rights, and then the rights may be given back. שמואל said one may not give up rights and then have them given back.
steps.whatsHappening: The word גופא tells us the גמרא is pausing the story with רבא. It now looks closely at the רב and שמואל ruling that was quoted there. This step sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 2–3 used this dispute as a tool in an argument. Now the dispute itself becomes the topic. The case is two people in one courtyard with no עירוב: one gives up his rights to the other, and then the second gives rights back to the first.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The matter itself': returning to look closely at a ruling quoted earlier
We give up (renounce) rights in the courtyard (ביטול רשות)
And then rights are given up again, back in the other direction

phrases.english: The matter itself: רב said:
phrases.notes: גופא means the גמרא is going back to a ruling it quoted earlier, to look at it on its own.

phrases.english: We give up rights, and then rights are given back again,
phrases.notes: First one person gives up his rights. Then the other person gives rights back to him.

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: אֵין מְבַטְּלִין וְחוֹזְרִין וּמְבַטְּלִין.
phrases.english: And שמואל said: we do not give up rights and then have them given back again.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the dispute quoted in steps 2–3 into its own topic of discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: rights may be given up and then given back. שמואל: they may not.

steps.title: Suggesting the dispute matches רבנן versus רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רב follows רבנן and שמואל follows רבי אליעזר in their dispute about someone who gives up courtyard rights.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that רב and שמואל are arguing about the same point as רבנן and רבי אליעזר? רב rules like רבנן, and שמואל rules like רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a suggestion. Maybe this new dispute is really just an older dispute in disguise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is an older dispute about a person who gives up his courtyard rights. רבי אליעזר says he gave up his house rights too, so he is completely out of the courtyard. That would fit שמואל: rights cannot be given back to someone who is no longer a resident. רבנן say he kept his house, so he is still a resident. That would fit רב: rights can be given back to him.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Shall we say?': introduces a suggestion that the גמרא will test, and often reject
A dispute
The Sages (the majority view)
They disagree

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two pairs. רב is linked to רבנן (rights can come back), and שמואל is linked to רבי אליעזר (the person is fully out). Also, a לימא is only a suggestion, not a final ruling.

phrases.english: Shall we say that רב and שמואל

phrases.aramaic: בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבָּנַן וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר קָא מִיפַּלְגִי.
phrases.english: are disagreeing about the same dispute as רבנן and רבי אליעזר?
phrases.notes: That dispute is about a person who forgot the עירוב and then gave up his courtyard rights: did he also give up his house?

phrases.english: That רב rules like רבנן,
phrases.notes: He kept his house, so he is still a resident. Rights can be given back to him.

phrases.english: and שמואל rules like רבי אליעזר.
phrases.notes: He gave up even his house, so he is fully out. Rights cannot be given back to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to link the dispute from step 6 to an older תנאים dispute.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the dispute between רב and שמואל simply the same as the dispute between רבנן and רבי אליעזר?

steps.title: רב can agree even with רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: רב says his ruling works even for רבי אליעזר. רבי אליעזר only said the house is included because people don't live in a house without a courtyard. He never said the person is fully removed from the courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב could say to you: I hold my view even according to רבי אליעזר. רבי אליעזר only said there that one who gives up his courtyard rights also gives up his house rights. That is because people do not live in a house without a courtyard. But did he say the person is completely removed from the courtyard?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion from step 7. It shows that רב does not have to disagree with רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר's reason is about what the person meant to give up. A house without a courtyard is useless, so giving up the courtyard clearly means giving up the house too. That does not mean the person stops being a resident who can later receive rights back, so רב's ruling still holds. The question at the end is rhetorical and means 'No, he never said that.'

keyTerms.meaning: 'He could say to you': introduces a possible reply on someone's behalf
'He only said this far': limits an opinion to its original case
Rights (in the courtyard or the house)
People live (in a place)
Being fully removed or taken out (from the courtyard)

steps.whatToRemember: The attempt to link the disputes fails. Giving up one's house along with the courtyard is about what the person intended. It does not mean he is fully removed from the courtyard. So even רבי אליעזר may allow rights to be given back, just as רב rules.
steps.confusionAlert: 'He gave up his house' and 'he is completely out of the courtyard' sound the same, but they are two different ideas. רב separates them.

phrases.english: רב could say to you:
What I said holds even according to רבי אליעזר:

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הָתָם
phrases.english: רבי אליעזר only said there
phrases.notes: This limits רבי אליעזר's ruling to its original case.

phrases.aramaic: הַמְּבַטֵּל רְשׁוּת חֲצֵירוֹ — רְשׁוּת בֵּיתוֹ בִּיטֵּל,
phrases.english: that one who gives up his courtyard rights has also given up his house rights,
because in a house without a courtyard
people do not live.
phrases.notes: So it is obvious he meant to give up the house too.

phrases.english: But regarding being completely removed (so rights cannot come back to him), did he say that?
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question meaning: he never said so.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְךָ רַב, אֲנָא דַּאֲמַרִי אֲפִילּוּ לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggested link from step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the claim that רב must disagree with רבי אליעזר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The suggestion treated 'he gave up the house' as if it meant 'he is fully removed from the courtyard.' רבי אליעזר's reason (people don't live in a house without a courtyard) only explains what was given up. It says nothing about being removed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common גמרא move: limiting an opinion to its exact reason, so that a later אמורא does not have to argue with a תנא.

steps.title: שמואל's ruling also fits רבנן
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rejects the idea that he must follow רבי אליעזר. רבנן only said that the house is not included in what he gave up. Whatever he did give up, he left completely.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל could say: My ruling fits even רבנן. רבנן only said that what he gave up is given up, and what he did not give up is not given up. But from whatever he did give up, he removed himself completely.
steps.whatsHappening: In step 8, רב showed that his ruling fits רבי אליעזר. Now שמואל does the same thing from the other side and shows that his ruling fits רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבנן said that giving up the courtyard does not automatically give up the house. שמואל says this only limits how much was given up. It does not mean the person kept a partial connection to the courtyard. For the courtyard itself, he is fully out, so the others cannot give the rights back to him.

keyTerms.meaning: They only said their ruling up to this point (and no further)
He gave up (renounced) his rights
He removed himself completely
At least, in any case

steps.whatToRemember: Both רב and שמואל can fit their rulings into either side of the dispute between רבי אליעזר and רבנן. So that dispute does not decide their argument.

phrases.english: And Shmuel could say:
What I said fits even the view of the Rabbis

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמְרִי רַבָּנַן הָתָם
phrases.english: The Rabbis only said there
that what he renounced is renounced
phrases.notes: This refers to the courtyard.

phrases.english: and what he did not renounce is not renounced
phrases.notes: This refers to the house.

phrases.english: But from what he did renounce
at least, he removed himself completely.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This parallels step 8. Now שמואל rejects the link that step 7 proposed for him.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: It rejects the claim that שמואל must follow רבי אליעזר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבנן only limited how much is given up. They never said the person keeps a partial hold on what he gave up.

steps.title: A dispute between תנאים about carrying after giving up rights
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת says the dispute between רב and שמואל is like a dispute between תנאים. The case is a person who gave up his rights and then carried into the courtyard. רבי מאיר says he forbids carrying even if he did it by mistake. רבי יהודה says he forbids it only if he did it on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר חנא said in the name of רב ששת: This is like a dispute between תנאים. If someone gave away his rights and then carried something out, whether by mistake or on purpose, he forbids carrying for everyone. These are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: on purpose, he forbids; by mistake, he does not forbid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an earlier source, an argument between תנאים, which might be the same as the argument between רב and שמואל. This step sets up the next move, where the גמרא explains how the two arguments match.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying from his house into the courtyard acts like taking his rights back, so carrying becomes forbidden for everyone. רבי מאיר says even a mistaken act takes the rights back. רבי יהודה says only a deliberate act does.

keyTerms.meaning: Like a dispute between תנאים
He gave away his rights (to the courtyard)
He carried out (from his house to the courtyard)
By mistake / on purpose
He makes carrying forbidden (for the others)

steps.confusionAlert: Here, "אוסר" does not mean the person did a forbidden act. It means his act makes carrying forbidden for all the other residents of the courtyard.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר חָנָא אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת,
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Chana said that Rav Sheshet said:
It is like a dispute between Tannaim:
One who gave away his rights and then carried out,
whether by mistake or on purpose, makes carrying forbidden
These are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
On purpose, he makes carrying forbidden;
by mistake, he does not make it forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר חָנָא אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת כְּתַנָּאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both attempts to tie רב and שמואל to רבי אליעזר and רבנן fail, the גמרא tries to tie them to a different dispute between תנאים.
steps.raayaObject: The dispute between רב and שמואל about giving up rights and getting them back
steps.raayaSupportSource: The dispute between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה about someone who carried after giving up his rights

steps.title: Proposing how the Tannaim's dispute matches רב and שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי מאיר holds you can give up rights and get them back, like רב. It suggests that רבי יהודה holds you cannot, like שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it not that this is what they argue about? One master holds that people may give up rights and then have them given back. The other master holds that people may not give up rights and then have them given back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains exactly how the argument between the תנאים would match the argument between רב and שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the person never fully left the courtyard, as רבי מאיר would hold, even a careless act can bring his rights back. That fits רב. If he fully left, as רבי יהודה would hold, only a deliberate act could undo it. That fits שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not that... (a suggested reading)
They argue about
People may give up rights and then give them back

phrases.english: Is it not that they argue about this:
One master holds that people may renounce and then renounce back
phrases.notes: This is רבי מאיר, matching רב.

phrases.aramaic: וּמַר סָבַר אֵין מְבַטְּלִין וְחוֹזְרִין וּמְבַטְּלִין.
phrases.english: and the other master holds that people may not renounce and then renounce back.
phrases.notes: This is רבי יהודה, matching שמואל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It explains the link that step 10 claimed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the dispute between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה is the same as the dispute between רב and שמואל

steps.title: רבא: the תנאים argue about a penalty, not about giving rights back
steps.stepSummary: רבא says everyone agrees that rights cannot be given back. רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה argue only about whether the חכמים penalized a mistaken act because of a deliberate one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר תחליפא said in the name of רבא: No. Everyone agrees that people may not give up rights and then have them given back. Here they argue about whether the חכמים penalized a mistaken act because of a deliberate one. One master holds they did penalize it. The other master holds they did not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proposed match. It explains the argument between the תנאים on a completely different basis.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both תנאים agree with שמואל that the person left completely. A deliberate act forbids carrying because of a penalty. רבי מאיר extends the penalty to a mistaken act so people will not confuse the two cases. רבי יהודה does not extend it.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
They (the חכמים) imposed a penalty
A mistaken act because of a deliberate act

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, the argument between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה is about a penalty (קנס). It is not about giving rights back. So this source also does not decide between רב and שמואל.
steps.whyThisMatters: Each attempt to find a source for רב and שמואל among the תנאים is pushed aside. This shows that their argument stands as its own question.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר תַּחְלִיפָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Tachlifa said in the name of Rava:
No, everyone agrees
that people may not renounce and then renounce back,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָכָא בְּקָנְסוּ שׁוֹגֵג אַטּוּ מֵזִיד קָא מִיפַּלְגִי.
phrases.english: and here they argue about whether they penalized the mistaken act because of the deliberate one.

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר: קָנְסוּ שׁוֹגֵג אַטּוּ מֵזִיד,
phrases.english: One master holds: they penalized the mistaken act because of the deliberate one,
phrases.notes: This is רבי מאיר.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: לֹא קָנְסוּ שׁוֹגֵג אַטּוּ מֵזִיד.
phrases.english: and the other master holds: they did not penalize the mistaken act because of the deliberate one.
phrases.notes: This is רבי יהודה.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אֵין מְבַטְּלִין וְחוֹזְרִין וּמְבַטְּלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It rejects the reading proposed in step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: It rejects the claim that רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה argue about the same issue as רב and שמואל.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The argument between the תנאים can be explained as a question about a penalty (קנס), so it need not be about giving rights back.

steps.title: רב אשי links רב and שמואל to רבי אליעזר and רבנן
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the argument between רב and שמואל really is the same as the argument between רבי אליעזר and רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: רב and שמואל are arguing in the same dispute as רבי אליעזר and רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי does not accept the earlier rejections. He says the two arguments really are the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רב and שמואל each claimed their view could fit both תנאים. רב אשי disagrees. According to רבי אליעזר, the person gives up his house too, so he is completely out of the courtyard, like שמואל. According to רבנן, he keeps his house and stays partly connected, so the others can give rights back to him, like רב.

keyTerms.meaning: A late אמורא who often gives the final word in a sugya
A dispute or argument
They are arguing

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב אשי, רבנן match רב (rights can come back), and רבי אליעזר matches שמואל (he is fully out).
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the pairs. רב matches רבנן, not רבי אליעזר. Earlier, רב had to explain how his view could fit even רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Rav and Shmuel

phrases.aramaic: בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְרַבָּנַן קָא מִיפַּלְגִי.
phrases.english: are arguing in the dispute of Rabbi Eliezer and the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: רַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְרַבָּנַן קָא מִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the comparison that steps 8 and 9 rejected, and says the comparison is correct.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument between רב and שמואל is the same as the argument between רבי אליעזר and רבנן.

steps.title: The משנה's story about a צדוקי neighbor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, where רבן גמליאל begins a story about a צדוקי who lived with them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל said: There was a story with a certain צדוקי who lived with us.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new line of the משנה. It quotes it to set up a question about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, the משנה only talked about living with a גוי. Now רבן גמליאל suddenly mentions a צדוקי. This sudden change is what the גמרא will ask about next.

keyTerms.meaning: A leading תנא and head of the סנהדרין
A story or real event
A Jew who rejected the תורה שבעל פה

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel said:
There was an incident with a certain Sadducee
who lived with us.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּצַדּוּקִי אֶחָד שֶׁהָיָה דָּר עִמָּנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן גמליאל tells a story about a צדוקי who lived in their alleyway.

steps.title: Why is a צדוקי mentioned at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבן גמליאל brings up a צדוקי when the משנה never mentioned one before.
steps.simpleTranslation: A צדוקי? Who mentioned his name?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a gap in the משנה. Nobody had talked about a צדוקי, so why is there a story about one?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A story in a משנה is usually brought to prove a rule that was already stated. Here there is no rule about a צדוקי for the story to prove. That makes the משנה look incomplete.

keyTerms.meaning: Who mentioned his name? (meaning: this topic was never brought up)

phrases.english: A Sadducee, who mentioned his name?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks a question about the line just quoted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A story about a צדוקי appears without any earlier rule about a צדוקי that it could support.

steps.title: The משנה is missing words: is a צדוקי like a גוי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that words are missing from the משנה. The תנא קמא says a צדוקי is like a גוי, and רבן גמליאל disagrees. He supports his view with the story of his father.
steps.simpleTranslation: Words are missing, and this is what the משנה teaches: A צדוקי is like a גוי. רבן גמליאל says: A צדוקי is not like a גוי. And רבן גמליאל said: There was a story with a צדוקי who lived with us in an alleyway in ירושלים. Father told us: Hurry and take the utensils out to the alleyway, before he takes his out and forbids it for you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fills in the missing part of the משנה. Now the story has a rule to support.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גוי cannot simply give up his rights. One must rent his rights from him. According to רבן גמליאל, a צדוקי is still a Jew, so he can give up his rights like any Jew. That is why his father told his sons to hurry and use the alleyway before the צדוקי took his utensils out and made carrying forbidden again.

keyTerms.meaning: Something is missing from the text
And this is what it teaches
Like a non-Jew
An alleyway shared by several courtyards
And he will forbid you (from carrying)

steps.confusionAlert: When רבן גמליאל says "Father," he means his own father. It is not a person named אבא.

phrases.english: It is incomplete (words are missing)
and this is what it teaches:
A Sadducee is like a gentile,
and Rabban Gamliel says:
A Sadducee is not like a gentile.
And Rabban Gamliel said:
There was an incident with a certain Sadducee
who lived with us
in an alleyway in Jerusalem,
and Father said to us:
Hurry and take the utensils out to the alleyway,
before he takes out (his)
and forbids it for you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by restoring the missing words of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Missing text (חסורי מיחסרא): restoring a lost line of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה never discussed a צדוקי, so the story seemed out of place.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה contains an argument over whether a צדוקי is like a גוי, and the story supports רבן גמליאל's view that he is not.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a צדוקי, according to רבן גמליאל, can give up his rights like a Jew. A גוי cannot do this and must rent out his rights instead.

steps.title: A ברייתא confirms the dispute about a Sadducee
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports the restored משנה. Its opening ruling is that a צדוקי and a ביתוסי forbid carrying like a גוי, and רבן גמליאל disagrees. It then tells the story of רבן גמליאל and his sons in the version reported by רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was taught in a ברייתא: One who lives with a גוי, a צדוקי, or a ביתוסי, they forbid carrying for him. (רבן גמליאל says: A צדוקי and a ביתוסי do not forbid.) There was a story with a צדוקי who lived with רבן גמליאל in an alleyway in ירושלים. רבן גמליאל said to his sons: My sons, hurry and take out what you want to take out and bring in what you want to bring in, before this loathsome one takes out and forbids you, since he gave up his rights to you. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא showing that this argument about a צדוקי really existed among the תנאים. This supports the missing words it added to the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא spells out the same argument: one view puts a צדוקי and a ביתוסי in the same group as a גוי, and רבן גמליאל disagrees. It also adds the reason for hurrying: the צדוקי gave up his rights to them. The sons wanted to use the alleyway before he could take that back.

keyTerms.meaning: And was it not taught in a ברייתא (introduces a supporting source)
A Boethusian, a sect similar to the Sadducees
They forbid carrying
This loathsome one
He gave up his rights

steps.whatToRemember: There is an argument among the תנאים about a צדוקי. One view treats him like a גוי, and רבן גמליאל says he is like a Jew and can give up his rights.

phrases.english: And was it not taught:
One who lives with a gentile, a Sadducee, or a Boethusian,
these forbid carrying for him.
(Rabban Gamliel says:
A Sadducee and a Boethusian do not forbid.)
And there was an incident with a certain Sadducee
who lived with Rabban Gamliel
in an alleyway in Jerusalem,
and Rabban Gamliel said to his sons:
My sons, hurry and take out
what you want to take out
and bring in what you want to bring in,
before this loathsome one takes out (his)
and forbids it for you,
since he gave up his rights to you;
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
phrases.notes: The words just before this, רבן גמליאל's 'hurry... before this loathsome one takes out,' are רבי מאיר's version; רבי יהודה gives a different one in the next step. Some versions leave out the words in round brackets.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: הַדָּר עִם הַנׇּכְרִי, צַדּוּקִי, וּבַיְתּוֹסִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to support the missing words added to the משנה in step 16.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה contains an argument over whether a צדוקי is like a גוי
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording the view that a צדוקי is like a גוי and רבן גמליאל's disagreement, along with the story of his sons (in רבי מאיר's version)

steps.title: רבי יהודה's version: Hurry before nightfall
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה reports that רבן גמליאל said something different: finish what you need in the מבוי before it gets dark, because then he will forbid you.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: רבן גמליאל said it with different words. 'Hurry and do what you need in the alleyway before it gets dark and he forbids it for you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from the last step continues. רבי יהודה gives his own version of what רבן גמליאל told his sons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי יהודה's version, the deadline is nightfall, when שבת begins. Once שבת starts, the צדוקי forbids carrying no matter what. In רבי מאיר's version, the deadline seems to be the moment the צדוקי himself carries.

keyTerms.meaning: With different wording; another version of the same story
Hurry
A shared alleyway that several courtyards open into
Before it gets dark, meaning before שבת begins
And he will forbid carrying for you

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה is not disagreeing about the story. He is giving a different version of רבן גמליאל's words, and that version changes when the danger begins.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
With a different wording:
phrases.notes: רבן גמליאל told his sons the following.

phrases.english: Hurry and do whatever you need in the alleyway
before it gets dark
phrases.notes: Before שבת begins.

phrases.english: and he forbids it for you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted in step 17 by adding רבי יהודה's version of רבן גמליאל's words.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רבי יהודה's version, the time limit is nightfall. Once שבת begins, the צדוקי forbids carrying in the מבוי.

steps.title: Quoting רבי מאיר's version for analysis
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי מאיר's version of the ברייתא again: carry what you need before this loathsome person carries and forbids you.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: 'Take out what you want to take out, and bring in what you want to bring in, before this loathsome person takes out his things and forbids it for you.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא quotes רבי מאיר's version of רבן גמליאל's words so it can question it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, the deadline is not nightfall but the moment the צדוקי carries. That wording suggests that what matters is who carries first. The next step picks up on exactly this.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Master said.' This phrase introduces a re-quote of an earlier source so the גמרא can analyze it.
Take out (carry from the house into the alleyway)
Bring in (carry from the alleyway into the house)
This loathsome person, meaning the צדוקי

phrases.english: The Master said:
Take out what you want to take out,
and bring in what you want to bring in,
before this loathsome person takes out his things
and forbids it for you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רבי מאיר's version from step 17 and quotes it again so it can be analyzed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר's version says the danger begins when the צדוקי carries, not when it gets dark.

steps.title: Does carrying first protect the alleyway?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges what רבי מאיר's version seems to imply: if the residents carry first and the צדוקי carries afterward, does he really not forbid it?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that to say that if they take out their things first, and then he takes out his, he does not forbid it?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is surprised by what רבי מאיר's wording implies. It asks whether whoever carries first on שבת really keeps the alleyway permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the words 'before he takes out' are read exactly, the residents are only in danger until the צדוקי carries. If they carry first, his later carrying would not forbid anything. The גמרא finds this hard to accept: רבי מאיר himself ruled (step 10) that one who gave up his rights and then carried out forbids carrying for everyone, even by mistake, so why should it matter who carried first?

keyTerms.meaning: 'Is that to say?' This word introduces a surprising conclusion drawn from a source.
They take out (carry outward)
And afterward
He does not forbid

steps.whyThisMatters: This question turns the story into a halachic question: does the order of who carries on שבת decide whether the alleyway is permitted or forbidden?

phrases.english: Is that to say
that when they take out their things first,
and afterward he takes out his things,
he does not forbid it?!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְּכִי מַפְּקִי אִינְהוּ וַהֲדַר מַפֵּיק אִיהוּ לָא אָסַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a surprising conclusion from the wording quoted in step 19 and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's version of רבן גמליאל's words: 'before this loathsome person takes out his things.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wording implies that carrying first protects the residents from the צדוקי's later carrying. That seems to contradict רבי מאיר's own ruling that one who gave up his rights and then carries out forbids carrying for the others.
